In this golf-inspired board game, each player must take action on the 9 cards on his or her course in order to score as few points as possible. For a 9-hole, the game is played in 28 actions. Each action is determined by the 28 shuffled action cards. May the best golfer win! Number of players: 1 - 8 Game duration: 8 mn Complexity: 2 / 5 Play Golfie and 1414 other games online. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Turn 3 Action Cards 4 Combos 5 Game End Overview Try to gain the lowest score across two rounds Turn An action card is revealed and all players must perform it After which, everyone checks to see if they have a Combo or a Lost Ball Action Cards Hole - This means you pick a card in the upper row (faceup or facedown) and reveal it before scoring its depicted value. After which, it is discarded, the column it was taken from is shifted up, and a new facedown card is drawn to fill the empty space Zone to Play - These cards look like your playing grid with a ball in the space relevant e.g. middle left. After locating the space, each individual player has a choice, you can either flip the card faceup if it were facedown, or you can exchange it with a card orthogonally adjacent to it. You are only forced to exchange if the card in the space has already been revealed. You do not have to exchange like for like, e.g. a faceup or facedown card can be exchanged with either a faceup or facedown card. Double Zone - This is like Zone to Play, except there are two spaces which must be actioned Golf Cart - This is like Zone to Play, except you can choose a single card from anywhere in your grid Lost Ball - Mark that it has come up on your scorecard in the +1 box, then draw again Combos A Combo is three cards which share the same value and aligned in a straight orthogonal line All three cards are removed and scored by placing a mark in the -2 box, then other cards are moved up to replace them before the lower empty spaces are refilled Game End When the Final Hole card is revealed for the first time, mark your score in the first score box, then play another round When the Final Hole card is revealed for the second time, mark your score in the second score box, then add both scores together to make your final score The player with the LOWEST score, wins! [Rating: 2/10] I don’t get the point of this game. It’s basically just flipping and moving cards to form combos, and it has absolutely nothing to do with golf despite the name. The gameplay is overly random and swingy due to constant card flips and luck-based placement. It’s one of the few games I didn’t even feel like finishing — just dull and pointless.

[Rating: 3/10] A card game where players are manipulating their 3x3 grid of face down cards and a event deck gets revealed one at a time containing actions (reveal cards, moving cards around, scoring a hole). If a row/column has the same number, player remove them and gain -2 bonus. Players continue until all 9 holes are filled in. Player with the lowest score wins. id rather play 'play nine'.

[Rating: 4/10] This is not a game aimed at me, but it was not appealing nonetheless. Very solitaire feeling.
